text:
The Islanders' trip west has turned into a long look at what happens when one player is doing too much. Ilya Sorokin made 37 saves in San Jose on Monday and lost in a shootout, with all seven New York shooters failing to score. Newsday's headline the next day said it plainly: the Islanders can't keep wasting his great nights. Sorokin is 8.2 goals saved above expected this season after 22.3 last year. The team in front of him is winless in four, outscored 17-9, and the chances agree: 43% of the expected goals in that run, the measure of who got the better looks.

Help may be close. Mathew Barzal, Matias Maccelli and Ryan Pulock all traveled on this trip, per Newsday, and Maccelli has an estimated return of Nov. 14. Until then the minutes have gone to Simon Holmstrom, up to 19:27 a night and on the top power play, and to Matthew Schaefer, the 19-year-old defenseman who plays his 100th NHL game and has become the reason to watch this team. Tony DeAngelo plays his 500th. Victor Eklund has goals in three straight.

Los Angeles is a strange case of its own. The Kings have 12 points in 16 games, but their chances say they should have closer to 18, and over their last five they have 59% of the expected goals while going 2-3-0. Darcy Kuemper is the gap: .878 and 5.0 goals saved below expected. He would play his 500th NHL game tonight, wearing his Hockey Fights Cancer mask for the rest of November, per LA Kings Insider. Juuse Saros shut them out 3-0 on Tuesday. Adrian Kempe passed Dustin Brown on the franchise list with a hat trick against San Jose last week.

Our Sleepers are both Kings: Corey Perry, with 3.6 expected goals in his last ten games on the third line (21% to score), and Quinton Byfield, whose line creates 4.02 expected goals per 60 (50% for a point). Los Angeles won the first meeting 3-2 in overtime. Our numbers have the Kings at 3.13 expected goals and the Islanders at 2.88.
headline: Sorokin keeps standing on his head for nothing
